archetype.name: Playoff Team (riding a hot goalie)
archetype.definition: A team that has climbed every year of its recent history and now drives play at even strength for the first time in that span, but whose record sits a few points ahead of that play because of close-game luck and one rookie-level-elite goaltender carrying the crease.

report.headline: Montréal's 5-on-5 growth is real; the 121-point pace is not
report.take:
The Canadiens have climbed year by year, from 55 standings points in 2021-22 to 106 last season, and at 11-3-3 they are second in the Atlantic behind Boston and sixth on the site. The real change this year is not the record. It is the underlying play. Every season in the history ran below 50% in expected-goal share, last year at 47.9%. This year they own 52.3% of the 5-on-5 expected goals and 52% of the shot attempts. A team that used to win on goaltending and bounces now out-chances opponents more often than not.

The record still runs ahead of that play. Their Pts vs Goal Diff of +3.8 is the best in the league, and several of the last ten games went past regulation. The 8-0-2 run behind the current position is built partly on 5-4 and 4-3 finishes. The 5-on-5 PDO of 103 and an all-situations shooting rate of 12.6%, against a league average of 11.6%, point the same way. Caufield has 11 goals on 57 shots, and the attack is converting at a rate that rarely holds. The goal differential of +8 and a Goal Diff / GP ranked ninth describe a good team, not one on pace for 121 points.

The team save % of .895 hides a sharp split. Jacob Fowler is first among the league's 69 goalies on the site's tab, with a .925 save %, 11.4 GSAx and two shutouts in ten starts. Jakub Dobes is 66th, at .847 and -6.5 GSAx in seven starts. The B- goaltending grade is an average of a star and a liability, and much of this season's fortune depends on how the starts are divided. Two other things the record covers for: a power play at 15.4% (28th, well under the league's 22.5%) and a defense that is only 17th in goals against and allows more shots than it takes.

The core that drives the 5-on-5 numbers looks sturdy. Lane Hutson logs 24.87 minutes with 17 points and a 59.9% xGF. Nick Suzuki has 15 points and a 58.9% xGF despite playing only 11 of the 17 games, and Bolduc, Danault and Evans all sit well above 55%. Expect the overtime luck and the shooting to cool, and the points pace with them. The team underneath should still finish comfortably in a playoff spot, especially if Fowler keeps most of the starts.

strengths.title: Finally winning the 5-on-5 battle
strengths.body: Montréal owns 52.3% of the expected goals and 52% of the shot attempts at 5-on-5. That is a clear step up from a history that never cracked 48%. It comes from the core: Hutson, Suzuki, Bolduc, Danault and Evans all post strong on-ice xGF shares. Because it is structural rather than shooting-driven, it is the part of the start most likely to last.

strengths.title: Fowler is the league's best goalie
strengths.body: Jacob Fowler ranks first of 69 goalies on the site, with a .925 save % and 11.4 GSAx in ten starts. He is the main reason the team's GSAx is seventh despite a weak backup. Ten starts is a small sample, and .925 is a high bar to hold, but his value is the clearest single edge on the roster.

strengths.title: Hutson anchors an A- blueline
strengths.body: Hutson plays 24.87 minutes a night, leads the team with 17 points and ranks 12th of 252 defensemen. He also posts a 59.9% xGF. His puck-moving is what tilts the ice, and the blueline grade rests heavily on him, with Dobson the only other regular above 52%.

concerns.title: Record inflated by close-game luck
concerns.body: A Pts vs Goal Diff of +3.8 is the highest in the league, and a 5-on-5 PDO of 103 says the bounces are going their way too. The club has run positive here in recent seasons, so some of it may be real late-game finishing. Still, the league-leading margin will shrink, and the 121-point pace will shrink with it.

concerns.title: Dobes starts are a liability
concerns.body: Dobes has an .847 save % and -6.5 GSAx in seven starts, 66th of 69 on the site. That drags the team save % down to .895. Every game he starts erases much of what Fowler builds, so the share of starts is the biggest lever on the defense's results.

concerns.title: Power play and shot suppression lag
concerns.body: The power play converts 15.4%, 28th and far below the league's 22.5%, even with Hutson, Caufield and Slafkovský on it. At the other end the team allows 28.1 shots a game (21st) and gives up more than expected to opposing centers. Last year's 23.1% power play suggests the man-advantage can recover. The shot volume against looks more stubborn.

trend.note: An 8-0-2 run over the last ten games has lifted the points % 0.165 above the season mark. But the last five came with 3.4 goals allowed a game, worse than the season rate, so the run is being won in shootouts of goals rather than by tightening up.

weekAhead.headline: Three top-twelve teams and two elite goaltending tandems in four games
weekAhead.body:
This is the hardest week of the season so far. Minnesota (2nd on the site) visits with the league's top defense, holding forwards furthest under their usual output. Then comes a trip to division leader Boston, third on the site and first in goalie GSAx. Colorado (10th) and the Rangers (12th) round it out. Three of the four opponents have save percentages in the league's top three, so the high-conversion offense behind the recent run will be tested directly.

The soft spot is Colorado. Its goalies rank 27th in GSAx and it gives up more than expected to centers, a chance for Suzuki and the middle of the lineup to cash in at home. The Rangers' 89.1% penalty kill, second in the league, makes it unlikely the struggling power play turns around on Long Island Sound's side of the trip. A split of the week would be a solid result. Who starts in goal against Minnesota and Boston matters most.

keyMatchups.title: Caufield against Minnesota's wall
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota allows the fewest forward points against expectation in the league and is first against wingers in particular. Caufield's 11 goals come from heavy volume, and the Wild's .912 save % makes this his hardest night of the week. Expect a low-event game where Fowler's form decides it.

keyMatchups.title: Hutson against Boston's suppression
keyMatchups.body: Boston ranks first at holding defensemen under their expected points and leads the league with 15.4 goalie GSAx. Its own 106.8 PDO is even higher than Montréal's, and its 48% CF says the Canadiens can control the puck. Whether that turns into goals against an A+ goaltending group is the question of the week.

keyMatchups.title: Colorado's leaky crease and middle
keyMatchups.body: Colorado is third in offense and third in shots a game, so this will be a track meet. But its goaltending sits 27th in GSAx, and it ranks 28th against centers. This is the game of the week Montréal's skaters can win outright.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Fowler or Dobes gets the Minnesota and Boston starts: the gap between them is bigger than the gap between Montréal and either opponent.

restOfSeason.body:
The 5-on-5 improvement and Fowler's play are the sustainable parts, and they make this a playoff team with home-ice upside in a crowded Atlantic. The league-best Pts vs Goal Diff, the 103 PDO and the 12.6% shooting are the parts that will fade. That points to a finish well short of the 121-point pace, somewhere in the 100 to 110 range. Scoring should settle a little below the current 3.59 a game.

Two things could push the ceiling up. One is a power play that recovers toward last year's level, which the personnel suggests is likely. The other is a goaltending split that leans hard on Fowler. The floor drops if Dobes keeps taking a large share of starts or if Fowler's .925 proves a hot ten-game run.
swingFactors: Fowler's share of starts and whether his .925 holds
How far the close-game luck and high shooting regress

confidence.note: 17 games, ten of Fowler's starts; the 5-on-5 trend is consistent but the sample is small.
